person_note: The controlling narrator is third-person omniscient. Multiple quote passages externally narrate characters and their thoughts, while the authorized opening independently demonstrates the same technique and explicitly embeds first-person direct thoughts within third-person narration. Whole-book descriptions corroborate that the narrator moves among several characters' minds rather than alternating grammatical persons. The isolated first-person devotional, lyrical, and reflective fragments are therefore local speech, quotation, or direct thought, not autonomous first-person sections. The main residual uncertainty is the exact speaker or boundary of a few clipped fragments, not the book-level narrative person.
